presentation_contract.warning: Schematic render only. Exact 10th-century street grid, quay line and defensive circuit remain unresolved.

900.title: Waterford / Veðrafjǫrðr c. AD 900
900.summary: 第一阶段 Viking occupation / longphort 语境。Waterford City & County Council 的历史综述记载 9 世纪中叶已有 longphort，并在 902 年一度被放弃；精确聚落范围和它与后来 Dundory 核心的空间关系仍未解决。
900.evidence: settlement presence stronger than mapped extent
buildings: timber occupation / longphort activity — generalized only
no fixed urban street pattern asserted
prohibitions: precise later Viking Triangle street grid

950.title: Waterford / Veðrafjǫrðr c. AD 950
950.summary: 914 年重新建立后的 10 世纪 Hiberno-Norse settlement。公开发掘综述把早期核心放在三角形岬地东端、后来的 Reginald's Tower / Dundory 一带；Bailey's New Street 的两条沟可能与该区域西缘防御有关，但其精确年代和完整线路不能确定。
950.defence: earthwork / ditch relationship plausible; exact circuit unresolved
buildings: craft / service structures — possible, not individually located
river-facing activity without a fixed quay line
prohibitions: exact Bailey's New Street ditch = AD950 wall claim

1000.title: Waterford / Veðrafjǫrðr c. AD 1000
1000.summary: 10 世纪末至 11 世纪初的过渡阶段。城市由东端核心向西发展的总体趋势有考古背景支持，但现有公开资料不足以给出 AD1000 的精确占地边界、街网和城防线路。
1000.defence: early defensive system present in concept; line unresolved
1000.evidence: development trend C; rendered envelope D

1050.title: Waterford / Veðrafjǫrðr c. AD 1050
1050.summary: 11 世纪木构城市证据明显增强。Arundel Square / Peter Street 发掘记录了 11 世纪结构、三开间木构住宅、路径与地块边界；但 Bakehouse Lane 城防沟的树轮年代集中在 AD1070–1080，因此不能把那条较晚防线直接回推到 AD1050。
prohibitions: Bakehouse Lane AD1070–1080 ditch as default AD1050 boundary

claims.claim: Waterford derives from the Old Norse name Veðrafjǫrðr.
A Viking base / longphort was re-established at Waterford in AD 914 after an interruption around AD 902.
The 10th-century Hiberno-Norse settlement is interpreted as centred on the eastern end of the triangular promontory around Dundory / the later Reginald's Tower area.
The form, date and size of Waterford's earliest quayside remain poorly known.
Arundel Square preserves late Viking urban evidence including 11th-century structures, a paved Peter Street surface, houses, paths and property boundaries.
Timbers from the Bakehouse Lane defensive ditch produced dendrochronological dates centred on AD 1070–1080.
